register.name: Gilt financing remit, 2026-27
register.detail: UK Debt Management Office · revision of 28 October 2026, Budget 2026 · net financing requirement £258.6bn, up £7.4bn from April · auctions £169.1bn, syndications £54.1bn, gilt tenders £12.6bn executed, £14.9bn unallocated · green gilts £12.0bn
register.note: Budget-wide; gilt sales up £4.4 billion from the April 2026 revision, with Treasury bills to contribute £8.0 billion
register.text: The plan for gilt sales by the UK Debt Management Office in 2026-27, revised at Budget 2026: conventional, index-linked and green gilts, for a net financing requirement of £258.6 billion. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Granton Waterfront regeneration, City of Edinburgh Council
register.detail: National Wealth Fund · announced 11 September 2026 · enabling works for phase one: land remediation, roads, utilities and public realm · part of a £1.3bn regeneration programme
register.note: Phase one brings 847 homes, including 214 new social houses, a new primary school and 14 retail units; expected to unlock a further £160 million of private investment
register.text: A National Wealth Fund loan to the City of Edinburgh Council for the enabling works of the first phase of Granton Waterfront, a development of around 3,500 energy-efficient homes. Of the first 847 homes, 214 are new social houses, and the phase includes a new primary school, which carries the shelter and education standards.

register.name: Social and Affordable Homes Programme, 2026 to 2036
register.detail: Homes England · ten-year programme · 33 strategic partners confirmed 25 August 2026, with grants from £96.4M to £350M each for homes outside London · further homes through continuous market engagement
register.note: The strategic partners are housing associations and the councils of Cambridge, Eastleigh and Newcastle
register.text: Government grant for new social and affordable homes in England over ten years, described by the Government as the largest investment in social and affordable housing in a generation. Homes England allocates it through strategic partnerships with housing associations and councils, which carries the shelter standard.

register.name: Community ENABLE Funding for community development finance institutions
register.detail: British Business Bank · funded by the Department for Business and Trade · up to £150M of lending expected over the first two years · £20M allocated to BCRS Business Loans, the sixth accredited lender, in 2026 · loans of £25,001 to £250,000
register.note: Allocated to community development finance institutions so far; BCRS lent £9.9 million to over 124 smaller businesses in the year to March 2025
register.text: A British Business Bank programme that funds social impact lenders, mainly community development finance institutions, to lend to smaller businesses that may struggle to borrow from mainstream lenders. Private investors are to be sought in a second phase; it carries the livelihood standard through enterprise and jobs.

register.name: 4⅝% Green Gilt 2037
register.detail: UK Debt Management Office · launched by syndication 10 March 2026, £6.25bn nominal at a yield of 4.7167% · due 7 March 2037 · latest auction 3 November 2026, £3.25bn, cover 3.38 times, yield 5.268% · £16.0bn nominal in issue
register.note: The third green gilt of the United Kingdom; orders of £80.6 billion at launch, with around 66% of the allocation to the UK domestic market
register.text: A green gilt of the United Kingdom, sold under the UK Government Green Financing Framework, first published in 2021 and updated on 26 November 2025, which sets out the expenditures that green gilts finance. The Debt Office plans £12.0 billion of green gilt sales in 2026-27, with the focus on re-opening this gilt; it is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Hull District Heat Network, Hull City Council
register.detail: National Wealth Fund · announced 21 October 2025 · repaid from the network’s operation · with a £15M Green Heat Network Fund grant and £1.5M of Levelling Up Partnership funding · built, operated and maintained by Vital Energi
register.note: Phase one serves council properties, educational establishments, development sites and homes
register.text: A National Wealth Fund loan to Hull City Council for the first phase of a low-carbon district heat network in the city. It carries the energy standard, with low-carbon heat for homes and public buildings.

register.name: Great British Energy solar panels for schools and NHS sites
register.detail: Great British Energy and government · awarded, announced 26 September 2025 · around £80M for some 200 schools and £100M for nearly 200 NHS sites · by 15 May 2026, 225 schools and colleges and 162 NHS sites had completed installations · a further £25M for up to 40 more NHS sites
register.note: Up to an estimated £360 million in lifetime net bill savings for schools, colleges and NHS sites, Great British Energy said in May 2026
register.text: Funding from Great British Energy and government to put solar panels on schools and NHS sites in England and cut their energy bills. It carries the energy standard, and the savings stay with schools and hospitals, which bears on the education and health standards.

register.name: Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund, Wave 3
register.detail: UK Government · allocated 11 March 2025 · 144 projects across England · announced with the Warm Homes: Local Grant, £500M to 73 projects across 270 local authorities over three years
register.note: Together the two funds can upgrade up to 170,000 homes in England, the Government says
register.text: Government grant to social housing landlords to upgrade the energy performance of social homes in England, which could help households save hundreds of pounds a year. It carries the shelter and energy standards, with warmer homes and lower bills for tenants.

register.name: Vanguard West and Vanguard East offshore wind farms (RWE and KKR)
register.detail: National Wealth Fund · 11 November 2026 · two £500M commitments · financial close reached for both projects · about £13bn of project-backed financing from a consortium of 35 international banks · Contracts for Difference from Allocation Round 7
register.note: 2.8 GW off the coast of Norfolk, enough for the equivalent of around three million UK homes; the release gives the package as £12.8 billion and as about £13 billion
register.text: Lending from the National Wealth Fund to two offshore wind farms off Norfolk, held 50:50 by RWE and KKR. It carries the energy standard, with clean power for the equivalent of around three million homes.

register.name: Sizewell C nuclear power station
register.detail: National Wealth Fund · term loan of up to £36.6bn for construction · final investment decision signed 22 July 2025 · construction cost around £38bn · Government stake 44.9%, La Caisse 20%, Centrica 15%, EDF 12.5%, Amber Infrastructure 7.6% · £5bn of proposed lending guaranteed by Bpifrance Assurance Export
register.note: The maximum envisaged exposure of the National Wealth Fund, whose lending was subject to contract and final due diligence when announced
register.text: The National Wealth Fund’s loan for the construction of Sizewell C, two EPR reactors with a planned capacity of 3.2 GW, which will provide the majority of the project’s debt. It carries the energy standard, with clean power for the equivalent of six million homes.

register.name: Resonance Housing Pathways Fund
register.detail: Resonance · open-ended residential property fund, launched in 2026 · target £700M by the end of 2030 · seeded with over £100M from two existing Resonance funds · projected net return of about 6% a year over 10 to 15 years
register.note: Initial investors include Better Society Capital, Oxfordshire Pension Fund (£10 million), Westminster City Council, City Bridge Foundation and five local and strategic authorities
register.text: An impact fund that buys homes for individuals and families who are homeless or in temporary housing, leased long term to housing partners such as Notting Hill Genesis and Salix Homes, with income backed by Local Housing Allowance rents. It aims to help around 15,000 people into stable housing over time, which carries the shelter standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

enterprises.heading: Already working in the United Kingdom.

items.name: Community Shop
items.text: A social enterprise of Company Shop Group that tackles the root causes of food insecurity through 17 stores in communities in the bottom 10% of the indices of deprivation, where members from the local area buy a weekly shop of deeply discounted food and essentials for around a third of the retail price.

items.name: Bath & West Community Energy
items.text: A community benefit society with 46 community-owned renewable projects of 16.54 MW, 39 of them rooftop solar on schools and other buildings, which raised £1 million in a community bond offer that closed on 27 May 2026 to build a 2 MW solar farm, and has given £470,000 to its fund for local projects that cut carbon and fuel poverty.

items.name: Golden Lane Housing
items.text: A charitable community benefit society and registered provider of social housing that gives people with a learning disability and autistic people safe and suitable homes, supporting over 2,800 tenants, and in February 2025 secured a £10 million revolving credit facility from Lloyds Bank for new homes and improvements in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

items.name: City Health Care Partnership CIC
items.text: A co-owned public service mutual that delivers over 50 healthcare services across Hull, the East Riding of Yorkshire and Merseyside, with a 93% patient satisfaction rate, named Social Enterprise Innovation of the Year at the UK Social Enterprise Awards 2025.

items.name: Peninsula Dental Social Enterprise
items.text: A social enterprise that works with the University of Plymouth’s dental school to improve oral health in the South West of England through treatment, education and engagement, named Public Services Social Enterprise of the Year at the UK Social Enterprise Awards 2025.

items.name: Change Please
items.text: A social enterprise that trains people experiencing homelessness as specialty baristas, pays them a Living Wage from day one and provides housing, mental-health support and onward job placement, funded by its cafés and wholesale coffee supply; it supports nearly 2,000 people a year and was named UK Social Enterprise of the Year 2025.

items.name: Social Enterprise Kent CIC
items.text: A community interest company across Kent and Medway that offers employability programmes, accredited training and health and wellbeing services, generating over £3 million a year that it reinvests locally and supporting more than 10,000 people each year.

items.name: EcoCoach CIC
items.text: A community interest company founded in 2024 that delivers trauma-informed physical education, wraparound care, alternative provision and inclusive sport in schools and communities, growing through trading with no reliance on grants, and named One to Watch at the UK Social Enterprise Awards 2025.
